readiness_fix_validation.mechanism: select on the underlying fd cannot see lines already prefetched by the buffered text reader. A coalesced noise+readiness burst therefore falsely times out; an incomplete line can also block beyond the requested timeout.
readiness_fix_validation.before_linux_real_pipe_test: Original upstream methods fail coalesced-burst readiness. This directly reproduces the code defect; it is not a claimed frequency estimate.
readiness_fix_validation.patch: Single reader thread owns the buffered output from startup; readiness is transferred through a bounded-time queue wait. No timeout increase, retry, image change or limit increase.
readiness_fix_validation.after_tests: 5/5 real-OS-pipe tests pass on Linux and Windows; existing sandbox unit tests 11/11 pass on Linux against the patched exact upstream copy. Cleanup exception changes are separate and excluded from this live validation.
readiness_fix_validation.after_cleanup: All four blocks return to 5 visible UID processes / 8 threads / 0 zombies. These are visible-process snapshots, not proof about all possible descendants or sites.
readiness_fix_validation.independent_audit: Manifest hashes, all 14 scheduled rows including failures/unstarted, return codes, kernel assertions, versions and scheduler costs cross-checked by verify_resource_diag.py. before-audit.json and after-audit.json retain both cohorts.
readiness_fix_validation.boundary: Fixed CPU task-image kernels, with one unused GPU reserved only because QOS requires it. No task/model training or MLE quality outcome. Sequential before/after live jobs are not randomized failure-rate estimates. The deterministic code defect is established; historical OpenBLAS resource-exhaustion cause is still unresolved.
